newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-KING OF CLAY PUTS DOWN ROOTS ON GRASS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KING OF CLAY PUTS DOWN ROOTS ON GRASS.

text.p: The long-held belief that Austria's Thomas Muster has an allergy to grass was finally dispelled on Thursday.
Tennis's so-called King of Clay has a new home and tennis court in Noosa Heads in Australia's Queensland tropical state.
"The surface is Rebound Ace (hardcourt), is it?" Muster was asked after the fifth seed's 6-3 6-2 6-2 second round victory over South Africa's Grant Stafford at the Australian Open on Thursday.
"Because it's easier to make it into a putting green when you don't like to play any more."

Since making his grand slam debut in 1985, Muster has not won a single match at Wimbledon, the world's main event on grass. Mostly he has given the tournament the cold shoulder, contesting it only four times.
Muster, the world number five, has 42 career singles titles mostly on clay court surfaces in Europe and even managed last year to reach the number one spot.
It is has been a running joke on the men's circuit that Muster must be allergic to grass, but now he has revealed otherwise.
"I just think it's nicer to play for family tennis," said the 1995 French Open champion.
"When I have guests they probably like to play more on grass, and it's better for your feet."
But he promptly added: "It's not that I'm going to win Wimbledon because of this."
Muster, born in the Austrian town of Leibnitz, said he plans to split his time between his homes in Monaco and Australia.
